posts.name: Technician (Fitter, Welder, Electrician, Diesel, AC, Machinist, Crane)

posts.name: Station Master
posts.note: Any degree + Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)

levels.note: Any recognised degree. Station Master has Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT).

stages.name: CBT 1 (Computer Based Test 1)
stages.tests: Graduate level (NTPC): 100 questions in 90 minutes. Undergraduate level: 100 questions in 90 minutes. ALP: 75 questions in 60 minutes.
stages.note: Qualifying in nature; the normalised score shortlists candidates to CBT 2. Negative marking 1/3.

stages.name: CBT 2 (Computer Based Test 2)
stages.tests: Graduate level (NTPC): 120 questions in 90 minutes. ALP Part 2: 125 trade-specific questions.
stages.note: Merit is prepared from the normalised CBT 2 score. ALP Part 2 must be qualified along with Part 1.

stages.name: Typing / Skill Test
stages.tests: Typing: 30 wpm English or 25 wpm Hindi, 10 minutes. Trade test for Technician as per the published trade syllabus.
stages.note: Qualifying only — does not add to merit.

stages.name: CBAT (Station Master / Goods Guard)
stages.tests: Five test batteries totalling about 90 minutes: memory, attention, perceptual speed, spatial visualisation, psychomotor.
stages.note: Qualifying. Only for Station Master and Goods Guard candidates who clear CBT 2.

stages.name: Document Verification + Medical
stages.tests: All original certificates, caste, domicile, NOC. Medical standard A-2 / B-1 / C-1 per post.
stages.note: Final appointment only after medical fitness.

ladder: Senior Section Engineer / Technician Gr. I (Level 5–6)

prepPlan.phase: Start the notification date is announced — Months 1–2
prepPlan.what: Do Class 9–10 NCERT Maths and Science first: that is exactly the level of General Science and most Maths questions. Add 30 minutes of GK daily (one newspaper plus one yearbook). Finish one textbook rather than starting five.

Move to reasoning type by type, leaving puzzles for last since they take the longest. Learn Maths shortcuts for percentages, interest, time-work and mensuration. Give a chapter-wise test after every topic.

One full timed CBT-1 mock every week. RRB gives about 54 seconds per question, so your target is under 55 seconds. Analyse every mock for silly mistakes — fixing errors alone moves cut-off marks more than new topics.
Two mocks a week plus a small revision notebook of formulae, GK facts and your own error log. Re-read the error log every week; it is the highest-return revision material you have.

Give mocks at the actual slot time so your body clock matches the exam. Stop new topics. Practise typing 15 minutes a day if the post needs the skill test, and start basic fitness because medical standards will be applied after the written stages.

reality: RRB recruitment runs on centralised employment notices (CEN). A single CEN can advertise tens of thousands of posts across the 21 RRBs.
CBT 1 is qualifying — clearing it does not guarantee a job. Several times the number of vacancies are called for CBT 2.
ALP Part 2 is trade-specific: non-ITI candidates fail it even with a good Part 1 score.
Station Master CBAT has no textbook preparation. Only timed psychometric practice helps.
Medical standards are strict. Colour vision rules out signal and telecom posts; BMI limits apply to some trades.
RRBs publish their own panels after centralised merit. You apply to one RRB per notice.

faq.q: How many Railway Recruitment Boards are there?
faq.a: 21 Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs), coordinated by the Railway Recruitment Control Board (RRCB) under the Railway Board, Ministry of Railways. Each RRB covers a group of zones. Confirm the current list at rrcb.gov.in.

faq.q: Can a 10th pass apply for Technician posts?
faq.a: No. Technician requires an ITI/NCVT certificate in the specific trade, and ALP requires the same or a diploma. A 10th pass applies for Level 1 posts such as Track Maintainer, Assistant Pointsman and Helper.

faq.q: What is the difference between RRB NTPC and RRB Group D?
faq.a: NTPC (Non-Technical Popular Categories) covers graduate and 12th-pass commercial and operating posts — Clerk, Station Master, Goods Guard, Typist. Group D covers Level 1 posts such as Track Maintainer, Helper and Pointsman. They are advertised in separate notices with separate exams.

faq.q: Is there negative marking in RRB exams?
faq.a: Yes. One-third of a mark is deducted per wrong answer in the computer based tests. There is no negative marking in the typing test, trade test or CBAT.

faq.q: Where do I find the official RRB notification?
faq.a: Each RRB website (for example rrbmumbai.gov.in, rrbchennai.gov.in), the central portal rrb.indianrailways.gov.in, and the coordinator rrcb.gov.in. SarkariJobs+ links the official PDF on every listing page.
You apply to one RRB per notice and your preference is within that board's zone group. The merit and panel are centralised, and the posting is made by the zone from its own vacancy list.
